title: mem0 config API -- T1552 unauthenticated plaintext API-key disclosure + Ollama-URL SSRF
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59706 (CVSS 9.2 CRITICAL),
documented by VulnCheck for mem0, an LLM memory-layer library.

mem0's config API exposes two unauthenticated endpoints with no
credential check. `GET /api/v1/config/` returns stored LLM provider
configuration, including API keys (e.g. OpenAI) in PLAINTEXT -- any
network caller can read them with no authentication. Separately,
`PUT /api/v1/config/mem0/llm` accepts a caller-controlled
`ollama_base_url` parameter that the server later uses to reach the
configured Ollama backend with no destination-address validation --
setting it to an internal address (e.g. a cloud instance-metadata
service) turns this into an SSRF primitive, letting an attacker pivot
from a public-facing mem0 deployment into the host's internal network
or cloud IAM credential endpoint.

Detection logic covers both halves of this advisory as two independent
selections: (1) a `GET /api/v1/config/` request with no Authorization
header, and (2) a `PUT /api/v1/config/mem0/llm` request whose
`ollama_base_url` value targets a private/link-local/metadata address
range -- each is exploitable on its own, so either alone is a hit
worth investigating.

Status correction (2026-09-04, live verification): the commit this rule
originally cited as "the fix" (`a3154d59e52386d4e1189c1f5f44819868f76514`)
is NOT a fix for this vulnerability -- its own commit message reads
"fix(docs): fix broken metadata filtering examples (#5317)", an unrelated
documentation change. The actual tracking issue, GitHub #6081, was closed
2026-07-06 with the maintainers' own comment: "we have sunsetted
openmemory, so we won't be taking issue or pr." This is WONTFIX-BY-
DEPRECATION, not a patched vulnerability -- the affected OpenMemory
component has been discontinued rather than fixed, so there is no
version number to check a deployment against; any still-running
OpenMemory instance remains exposed indefinitely by the vendor's own
choice not to patch a sunset product.

Aggregated from 2 independent sources (VulnCheck's write-up + the
project's own GitHub issue tracker, corroborating the wontfix status).
